note: The corpus that has been used to get script past sanitizers, and the shapes
specific to markdown itself. One file, read by both halves: the server's
submission check and the interface's renderer.
It was two hand-kept lists, and the Go one called itself 'the same corpus'
while being 27 payloads shorter. Two copies of a security corpus diverge in
the direction of the one nobody is adding to.
'submission' is what internal/markdown.Check must answer. Not every payload
is refusable there and saying so is the point: a fenced block holds whatever
it holds, and escaped text is text. Every payload, refused or not, must
render inert — that half is asked of the renderer, in web/src/ui.
